text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Wallis inquiry into the financial system has highlighted a deep division between the Federal Treasury and the Reserve Bank over the issue of prudential control. The Treasury advocates moving to a system where banks would no longer be seen as "special", removing perceptions that their depositors were protected by the government, while the Reserve Bank warns that this full-blown Treasury model could put at risk the stability of Australia's financial system. Page 1.

In a deal which illustrates the strength of foreign investors' interest in Australian banks and opens the way for unlimited business opportunities worldwide for Macquarie Bank, the bank announced yesterday that the government-owned Brunei Investment and Commercial Bank had paid A$152 million for a 13.4 percent stake in Macquarie. Page 1.

As investors prepare bids for the Federal Airports Corporation's first three airports, FAC has reported a 25.1 percent increase in earnings before abnormals to A$160.5 million. Sydney Airport returned the best performance in the group with a 32.5 percent rise in profit to a record A$91 million, while Melbourne airport and Brisbane airport appeared a little shaky. Page 2.

Unveiling its latest industry development results in Canberra yesterday, Telstra reported increased spending on products and services to small and medium-sized Australian enterprises in the past financial year, with an increase of A$200 million to A$1.4 billion. Telstra said it traded with more than 10,000 suppliers during the year, with about 1,000 of these receiving orders of more than A$300,000. Page 5.

As part of its European development strategy, Brambles Industries Ltd announced yesterday its U.K. joint venture with GKN Plc, the Cleanaway Group, will pay A$110 million to acquire German environmental services and waste management company Mabeg GmbH. The Mabeg deal is the first of three major acquisitions planned by the industrial group this year. Page 19.

Because of a difference of opinion with the board on the gross margins the business should maintain, clothing manufacturer and retailer Palmer Corp has sacked Michael Ford as managing director but will keep him in the company to help develop stratgies for marketing its brands in offshore markets. Palmer Corp also announced yesterday it had lifted sales 19 percent in the first quarter. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A letter sent by the Insurance and Superannuation Commission to the chief executives of 37 life insurance companies this month says the industry is struggling to uphold its new code of conduct and slams multi-agents and securities dealers for failing to meet industry standards, a finding which could have a bearing on the future of the ISC inside the Wallis inquiry into the financial system. Page 25.

Following the release of the latest Federal Airports Corp annual report, tabled in Parliament, which shows the group's network of 22 airports had reported a sharp jump in profit resulting from strong performances by major capital city airports, Australia's airports sell-off should attract a multi-million dollar price tag. Page 25.

Speaking after the Premier Investments annual meeting yesterday, chairman Harry Cooper, like Solomon Lew before him, denied yesterday he had any knowledge in 1990 that Coles Myer was behind the Yannon deal, and said he believed the Coles superannuation fund was the purchaser of the relevant preference shares in Premier. Page 25.

As part of a plan by Westpac director of institutional and international banking David Morgan to put the bank back on the frontline in Asia, the bank will today announce a major expansion of its operations in the region, which sources believe will see a strengthening of the commercial alliance which will extend the range of trade finance and retail services it can offer in Asia. Page 25.

It is understood Ten Group shareholders Robert Whyte and Jack Cowin - who each have a five percent stake - are considering following the lead of John Singleton Advertising Ltd, which in October offered its five percent stake for sale at A$13 a share, and are reviewing options to gauge market demand for their combined A$120 million-plus stake. Page 27.

A Price Waterhouse study commissioned by the Australian Telecommunications Industry Association has revealed industry programs axed or downgraded in the budget generated an additional A$1.5 billion in turnover and exports in the telecommunications sector last year. Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Macquarie bank announced yesterday that Brunei Investment Agency has become the biggest shareholder in the bank, Australia's only home-grown investment bank, after spending A$152 millon to buy a 13.4 percent holding from British merchant bank Hill Samuel. Page 27.

Australia's top five gold producers - Normandy Mining, Newcrest, Acacia Resources, Plutonic and Goldfields - have suffered a A$3.2 billion drop in their market capitalisation since the start of the year due to a slump in the industry resulting from the combined impact of a lower international gold price, a stronger Australian dollar and lower inflation expectations. Page 27.

The Rothwells saga - which took 14 months, 200 witnesses, 15,000 exhibits and cost an estimated A$10 million to finalise - drew to a close yesterday with the West Australian Supreme Court jury finding Peter Lucas, one of the bank's directors, and auditor Louis Carter guilty on one charge of concealing the true nature of Rothwells accounts and four charges of knowingly making false statements. Page 27.

Speaking at yesterday's annual shareholders' meeting, Harvey Norman executive chairman Gerry Harvey said that since June 30 sales had risen 11.4 percent to A$361.9 million and the retailer could expect sales growth of up to 16 percent for the year ahead although a cool December could play havoc with the estimates. Page 29.

According to a Coopers and Lybrand analysis which questions the level of cost savings arising from major bank mergers, regional banks are better equipped than their major bank counterparts to rationalise their branch networks successfully and attack their cost base without losing customers. Page 29.

Following a decision by its two percent shareholder, the Seven Network, to take legal action against pay-TV group Optus Vision's other three shareholders over an alleged breach of the shareholders' agreement, Optus has been forced to increase its short-term banking facility from A$280 million to A$700 million - to be provided by the ANZ, Deutsche Bank and Toronto Dominion Australia. Page 29.
THE AGE

Macquarie Bank announced yesterday the Brunei Investment and Commercial Bank had spent A$152 million acquiring a 13.4 percent stake in the Sydney-based investment bank, buying the entire stake held by Hill Samuel, Macquarie's previous parent company, at A$7.60 a share. Page C1.

Former Rothwells merchant bank director Peter Lucas and auditor Louis Carter face jail terms of up to seven years after the West Australian Supreme Court found them guilty yesterday of one charge of concealing the true nature of Rothwells' accounts and charges of knowingly making false statements. The conspiracy also allegedly involved Rothwells director Tom Hugall and its chairman Laurie Connell, who are both deceased. Page C1.

Just Jeans managing director Peter Wilkinson yesterday warned shareholders at the annual meeting that sales would be significantly lower during the first half and much rested on sales over Christmas. However, Wilkinson said the signs were not encouraging and the summer season was not showing consumer demand equal to last year. Page C1.

After Premier Investments annual meeting yesterday, executive chairman Harry Cooper said Premier had nothing to do with the controversial Yannon deal and it could boost its 5.26 percent stake in Coles "at the right time". Premier is controlled by Coles Myer director Solomon Lew. Page C3.

Coca-Cola Amatil stock dropped another 73 cents to a seven-month low of A$13.42 yesterday with almost A$500 million more being wiped from the beverage group's market capitalisation as analysts further downgraded earnings expectations for the company. Page C3.

The Australian art market took a slight jump upwards last night as 52 percent of the 164 lots offered at a Christie's auction were sold for a turnover of A$2.6 million. Arthur Boyd's Bridgeroom Drinking from a Creek II was sold for A$222,500 to a telephone bidder and Peter Russell's Madam Sisley on the Banks of the Loing was handed over to a Brisbane dealer for A$200,500. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
